players.product: photonic fault-tolerant quantum computers; Inception photonic chip manufacturing facility (Toronto, 158,000 sq ft)

quarterly_data.signal: Xanadu 20-F: 2025 revenue was US$4,617 thousand (2024: US$1,589 thousand), up 191% - professional services US$4,218 thousand and compute and other services US$399 thousand; Q4 2025 revenue US$1,875 thousand (+164%); net loss US$70,667 thousand, adjusted EBITDA US$(50,774) thousand; cash and cash equivalents US$16,164 thousand at December 31, 2025; approximately US$5,154 thousand of revenue expected from remaining performance obligations, all within the next 12 months.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue US$4,617 thousand (+191%); net loss US$70,667 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Xanadu 20-F: three customers accounted for 78% of 2025 revenue (44%, 20% and 14%); two customers accounted for 63% of 2024 revenue (53% and 10%); by customer location 2025 revenue was United States US$3,545 thousand, Canada US$814 thousand and rest of world US$258 thousand (approximately 77%, 17% and 6%).
quarterly_data.figure: three customers 78% of 2025 revenue (44%, 20%, 14%); U.S. approximately 77%

quarterly_data.signal: Xanadu 20-F: capital expenditures on property, plant and equipment were US$6.2 million in 2025 (2024: US$4.8 million), targeted at expanding its packaging facility and specialized test equipment, plus US$2.7 million of IP investments; it anticipates substantial capex in coming years for its R&D roadmap, scaling photonic integrated circuit fabrication processes and building the modular quantum racks required for utility-scale systems; purchase obligations of US$4.2 million are mainly R&D expenses payable to strategic suppliers.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 capex US$6.2 million (2024: US$4.8 million); US$4.2 million purchase obligations

quarterly_data.signal: Xanadu 20-F: its next-generation architecture targets scaling up to 100,000 physical qubits and up to 500 logical qubits in 2029-2030; it says its Aurora system (2025) demonstrated the first known integration of the subsystems required for universal quantum computing using photonics, and that its system computes at room temperature at telecom wavelengths so it can be deployed in conventional data-center environments.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 100,000 physical qubits and 500 logical qubits in 2029-2030

quarterly_data.signal: Xanadu 20-F: Xanadu currently supplies a major defense contractor (not named) with its photonic integrated circuits to support a U.S. government quantum-sensing program, and its low-loss photonic packaging technology is exploring pilot projects with external partners in classical communications; it sources PICs, superconducting transition edge sensors, photon-number-resolving detectors, optical fiber and electro-optic switches from a limited number of specialized suppliers, without long-term supply agreements with all of them.
U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory: Xanadu 20-F - Xanadu participates in programs with the U.S. Air Force Research Laboratory and with DARPA through the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative.
